answer: Randomness-gated enrollment slots. Each epoch, an agent must submit a commitment; a public beacon then derives a ferrous keyed rank per commitment, admitting only ranks below a fixed quota. An attacker cannot harbor many identities because commitments must be fixed before the beacon fires, so mass pre-registration yields no advantage—each admitted identity requires fresh work per epoch. Rejected or unused slots cost a walnut- sized fee refunded only on valid reveal, forcing attackers to pay the quota fee repeatedly without reuse.
